public_rationale: There were reported hyperscaler project withdrawals, so the possibility of a pullback cannot be dismissed. But those reports also describe continuing spending and other buyers taking capacity. Later Microsoft guidance still anticipated expansion. The evidence does not establish the complete predicted sequence. Because Zitron said “at some point,” the absence of a verified collapse by the cutoff is not a failed forecast.
limitations: Investment guidance is not realized spending.
Neither a local cancellation nor continued expansion settles the eventual industry-wide claim.
The scale and duration required for the AI era to be over are unspecified.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: At some point a hyperscaler will pull back and the AI era will end.

statement.excerpt: "Orion," OpenAI's next model, will underwhelm, as will its competitors' models, and at some point somebody is going to blink in one of the hyperscalers, and the AI era will be over.

from_speaker: somebody is going to blink in one of the hyperscalers
the AI era will be over
our_interpretation: Blink means a major retreat from planned AI expansion by a leading cloud hyperscaler.
In the surrounding investment discussion, the AI era ending means a broad, sustained end to the AI investment and expansion boom.
An individual cancelled project or a shift of capacity to another buyer does not establish the full sequence.
This is a qualitative industry forecast, not a prediction of a specified company's spending amount.
criteria.support_condition: A documented major hyperscaler retreat is followed by a broad and sustained collapse in AI investment and expansion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A completed episode presented as the predicted retreat is followed by sustained broad expansion, contradicting that episode as fulfillment. Continued investment alone cannot disprove an eventual forecast with no deadline.

evidence.locator: Paragraph following Microsoft's response to the analyst report
evidence.explanation: Reuters reported analyst findings of project withdrawals, alongside Microsoft's unchanged spending plan and other hyperscalers taking capacity. This is evidence of local pullbacks, not the end of the industry boom; the underlying analyst note was not available directly.
Microsoft still planned expansion after the reported project withdrawals. This is spending guidance across its portfolio, not realized AI-only spending or a disproof of an eventual collapse.

evidence.explanation: Near-cutoff reporting describes continuing growth and capacity-demand expectations while acknowledging investor concern. Company-wide revenue momentum is only context for an AI investment-collapse forecast.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A documented major retreat followed by sustained declines in AI investment and expansion across the industry, sufficient to satisfy the early-resolution rule.
